title: December 2026 Holidays and Celebrations Worldwide
summary: See when Hanukkah, Christmas, Kwanzaa, and other December 2026 holidays fall, and explore how families in the U.S. and around the world celebrate.
body_markdown:
***Quick answer:** Christmas Day falls on Friday, December 25, 2026, and is the only U.S. federal holiday that month. Hanukkah runs from sundown on December 4 through nightfall on December 12. Kwanzaa begins December 26 and continues through January 1, 2027, and New Year’s Eve falls on Thursday, December 31. Other celebrations include Día de las Velitas in Colombia (December 7), Las Posadas (December 16–24), and Rizal Day in the Philippines (December 30).*


**December is one of the busiest months on the calendar, and not just because of Christmas. Families across the U.S. mark the month with traditions rooted in dozens of cultures and faiths, from Hanukkah candle lighting to Las Posadas processions to Rizal Day commemorations in the Philippines. If you have loved ones celebrating in another country, knowing when these dates fall can help you plan calls, gifts, or a visit home.**


**This guide lays out the full December 2026 calendar, explains the traditions behind each date, and offers a few ways to feel close to family celebrating from afar.**


## December 2026 holidays and celebrations at a glance


**December 2026 date** **Holiday or celebration** **Where or how it’s observed**


Tue., Dec. 1 GivingTuesday A day of giving and volunteering in the U.S. and around the world.


Wed., Dec. 2 Eid Al Etihad (UAE National Day) Marks the formation of the United Arab Emirates.


Fri., Dec. 4–Sat., Dec. 12[Hanukkah](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/hanukkah/) Jewish Festival of Lights. The first candle is lit Friday evening, December 4.


Sat., Dec. 5 Sinterklaas Eve Gift-giving on December 5 in the Netherlands.


Mon., Dec. 7[Día de las Velitas](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/what-is-dia-de-las-velitas-colombias-festival-of-lights/) ,[La Gritería](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/what-is-la-griteria-nicaraguas-december-7-celebration/) Colombia lights candles and lanterns, Nicaraguan communities gather at Marian altars.


Tue., Dec. 8 **[Feast of the Immaculate Conception](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/feast-of-the-immaculate-conception/)** Catholic feast connected to the December 7 traditions in Colombia and Nicaragua.


Thu. evening, Dec. 10[Regaib Kandili](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/regaib-kandili-what-it-means-and-how-its-observed/) A night of prayer observed in Türkiye and in some Turkish Muslim communities abroad.


Sat., Dec. 12[Our Lady of Guadalupe](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/our-lady-of-guadalupe-day/) and[Jamhuri Day](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/jamhuri-day-celebration/) A Catholic feast with particular significance in Mexico and Mexican American communities, and Kenya’s national day.


Wed., Dec. 16[Bangladesh Victory Day](https://www.remitly.com/blog/en-ae/culture/how-does-the-uaes-bangladeshi-community-celebrate-victory-day/) A national commemoration in Bangladesh.


Wed., Dec. 16–Thu., Dec. 24[Las Posadas](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/las-posadas/) and **[Simbang Gabi](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/simbang-gabi-traditions-and-sending-money-to-the-philippines/)** Las Posadas is observed in Mexico and other communities. Simbang Gabi is a Filipino series of nine Masses, traditionally held before dawn. U.S. parish schedules can vary.


Mon., Dec. 21[December solstice](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/winter-solstice-traditions/) and **[Yalda Night](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/yalda-night-dates-meaning-and-traditions/)** The winter solstice in the U.S. and a night of family gatherings in Iranian and Afghan traditions.


Thu., Dec. 24 Christmas Eve,[Nochebuena](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/noche-buena-celebrations/) , and[Wigilia](https://www.remitly.com/blog/en-gb/culture/wigilia-how-britains-polish-community-celebrates-christmas-eve/) Christmas Eve celebrations include Nochebuena in many Latino and Filipino families and Wigilia in Poland.


Fri., Dec. 25 Christmas Day and[Quaid-e-Azam Day](https://www.remitly.com/blog/en-ae/culture/quaid-e-azam-day-in-the-uae-how-pakistanis-honour-muhammad-ali-jinnah-abroad/) Christmas Day is a U.S. federal holiday. Pakistan also marks the birthday of its founder, Muhammad Ali Jinnah.


Sat., Dec. 26 Boxing Day,[Bahamian Junkanoo](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/what-is-jonkonnu-the-caribbeans-colorful-christmas-street-festival/) , and[the first day of Kwanzaa](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/celebrating-kwanzaa/) The U.K. has a Boxing Day substitute bank holiday on Monday, December 28. The Bahamas celebrates Junkanoo on Boxing Day. Kwanzaa continues through January 1.


Mon., Dec. 28[Día de los Santos Inocentes](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/what-is-dia-de-los-santos-inocentes-the-hispanic-worlds-april-fools-day/) A Christian observance also associated with practical jokes in Spain and parts of Latin America.


Wed., Dec. 30 Rizal Day A Philippine public holiday honoring José Rizal.


Thu., Dec. 31[New Year’s Eve](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/new-year-around-the-world-who-celebrates-first/) U.S. countdowns, Scotland’s Hogmanay, Spain’s 12 grapes, and Japan’s Ōmisoka.


## When does Hanukkah start in December 2026?


[Hanukkah begins at sundown on Friday, December 4, 2026](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/hanukkah/) , and continues through nightfall on Saturday, December 12. Some calendars list December 5 as the start date, since that’s the first full day of the holiday, but families planning dinner or candle lighting should mark Friday evening as the real starting point ([Chabad.org](https://www.chabad.org/) ).


Over eight nights, families light the menorah, spin the dreidel, and share fried foods like latkes to commemorate the rededication of the Second Temple in Jerusalem. The holiday’s name, which means “dedication” in Hebrew, reflects its central theme: celebrating light and resilience during the darkest stretch of the year.


## How do Colombia and Nicaragua celebrate on December 7?


Two distinct but related traditions share this date. In Colombia,[Día de las Velitas (“Day of the Little Candles”)](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/christmas-in-colombia/) kicks off the Christmas season as families light candles and paper lanterns outside their homes, along sidewalks, and in public plazas. The glow marks the eve of the[Feast of the Immaculate Conception](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/feast-of-the-immaculate-conception/) , which falls the next day, December 8.


In Nicaragua,[La Gritería brings neighbors together at decorated altars to the Virgin Mary](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/what-is-la-griteria-nicaraguas-december-7-celebration/) . Participants call out “¿Quién causa tanta alegría?” (“Who causes so much joy?”), and the crowd answers with song and praise. Both customs set the tone for the weeks of celebration that follow.


## What happens on Our Lady of Guadalupe Day, December 12?


December 12 holds deep meaning in Mexico and in Mexican American communities throughout the U.S.[The Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe honors an apparition of the Virgin Mary](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/our-lady-of-guadalupe-day/) and is marked with Masses, processions, and serenades known as mañanitas. If you’d like to find a local celebration, many U.S. parishes post their December 12 schedules in advance, so checking with a nearby church is a good place to start.


December 12 is also[Jamhuri Day in Kenya](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/jamhuri-day-celebration/) , the country’s national day commemorating its founding as a republic.


## Why do Las Posadas and Simbang Gabi share the same stretch of December?


From December 16 through 24, two traditions from different parts of the world run side by side.[Las Posadas reenacts Mary and Joseph’s search for shelter](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/las-posadas/) before Jesus’s birth. Communities in Mexico and beyond reenact the journey through processions, songs, and gatherings at different homes each night.


**[Simbang Gabi](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/simbang-gabi-traditions-and-sending-money-to-the-philippines/)** , a Filipino tradition, consists of nine consecutive Masses, traditionally held before dawn, leading up to Christmas. Because U.S. parish schedules vary by location, it’s worth checking with a local Filipino or Catholic community for exact Mass times ([USCCB](https://www.usccb.org/) ).


## What is Yalda Night, and when does it fall in 2026?


The[December solstice arrives on Monday, December 21, 2026](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/winter-solstice-traditions/) , marking the longest night of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. For Iranian and Afghan families, that night is also[Yalda Night (Shab-e Yalda)](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/yalda-night-dates-meaning-and-traditions/) , a celebration of light overcoming darkness.


Families gather to share pomegranates and watermelon, recite Persian poetry, often from the poet Hafez, and stay up late telling stories. The symbolism is simple: the longer the night, the greater the joy when morning finally comes.


## How do families in Haiti, Ghana, and Vietnam celebrate Christmas?


Christmas traditions look different depending on where you are in the world. In Haiti, Christmas Eve is associated with fanal lanterns, handcrafted paper lanterns that light up homes and streets during the holiday season. In Ghana, Christmas is largely about homecoming, with many people traveling back to family villages to reunite with relatives they may not see the rest of the year. In Vietnam, cities light up with elaborate holiday displays, and some Christian communities attend Christmas Eve or Christmas Day services.


## What do people celebrate after Christmas?


### What are Kwanzaa, Boxing Day, Junkonnu, and Jonkonnu?


[Kwanzaa begins on Saturday, December 26](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/celebrating-kwanzaa/) , and continues through Friday, January 1, 2027. The weeklong celebration honors African American heritage and community values.


Boxing Day, also December 26, is widely observed in the U.K. and other Commonwealth countries. Because December 26 falls on a Saturday in 2026, the U.K. has designated a substitute bank holiday for Monday, December 28 ([GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/) ). In the Bahamas, Boxing Day is also the first of two Junkanoo parade days (the second falls on New Year’s Day), featuring elaborate costumes, music, and dancing through the streets. Jamaica has its own related tradition, Jonkonnu, featuring masked street performers during the Christmas season.


### What is Día de los Santos Inocentes, and who was José Rizal?


[Día de los Santos Inocentes](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/what-is-dia-de-los-santos-inocentes-the-hispanic-worlds-april-fools-day/) , observed December 28, has religious origins but is widely associated with practical jokes and pranks in Spain and parts of Latin America, similar to April Fools’ Day in the U.S. ([gob.mx](https://www.gob.mx/) )


Rizal Day, observed December 30, is a Philippine public holiday honoring José Rizal, a national hero whose writing and advocacy helped inspire the Philippine independence movement.


### How is New Year’s Eve celebrated around the world?


**[In the U.S., New Year’s Eve on Thursday, December 31](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/new-years-eve/)** , typically means countdowns, fireworks, and gatherings with friends and family. Elsewhere, the traditions vary widely. In Spain, people eat 12 grapes at midnight, one for each chime of the clock, for good luck in the year ahead. Scotland’s Hogmanay celebration includes fire festivals and first-footing, where the first guest to cross the threshold after midnight is said to bring luck. In Japan, Ōmisoka is marked with a thorough house cleaning and a bowl of toshikoshi soba noodles, eaten to “cross over” from one year to the next.


## How can I celebrate December holidays with loved ones who live abroad?


Distance doesn’t have to get in the way of marking these dates together. A few simple ideas can help:


- **Look up a local celebration.** Many U.S. cities host public Hanukkah lightings, Las Posadas processions, or Kwanzaa events that let you connect with a wider community.
- **Cook together over video.** Walking through a family recipe over a video call, whether it’s latkes, tamales, or Wigilia dishes, brings a shared tradition into two homes at once.
- **Send a gift or contribution ahead of time.** If you’re sending money to loved ones abroad for the holidays, **[Remitly supports transfers to more than 175 countries](http://www.remitly.com/)** , so your gift can arrive before the celebration starts. Check the estimated arrival date when you send, and if someone will be picking up cash in person, confirm local holiday hours first.


## Mark your December 2026 calendar


December 2026 brings a packed calendar of holidays, feast days, and celebrations spanning continents and faiths. Whether you’re lighting a menorah, walking in a Las Posadas procession, or planning a New Year’s Eve countdown, knowing these dates ahead of time makes it easier to join in, wherever your loved ones are celebrating.


## Frequently asked questions


### What federal holidays fall in December 2026?


Christmas Day is the only one. It falls on Friday, December 25, 2026 ([opm.gov](https://www.opm.gov/) ).


### Why do some calendars say Hanukkah starts on December 5?


The first night of Hanukkah begins at sundown on Friday, December 4. December 5 is the first full day of the holiday, which is why some calendars list it as the start date ([Chabad.org](https://www.chabad.org/) ).


### Are Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve U.S. federal holidays?


Neither date appears on the published 2026 federal holiday schedule. Employers and local services may set their own hours around these dates, so it’s worth checking in advance ([opm.gov](https://www.opm.gov/) ).


### When does Kwanzaa end?


Kwanzaa ends on Friday, January 1, 2027.
